title: "Reference"

description: "Reference for each Lua module of quarto-lua-modules: its functions, what they return, and what they do."
---

Each section below names one module.
Load a module with the path in [Vendoring](vendoring.qmd), and call its functions through the table it returns.

A module that loads a sibling needs that sibling copied too.
The table at the top of [Vendoring](vendoring.qmd#copy-the-modules-a-module-needs) lists them.

## colour.lua

Converts CSS colours to HTML hex, and reads the colour an attribute sets.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is_named_colour(value)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the value is one of the 148 CSS named colours. The match ignores case. |
| `expand_hex_colour(hex)` | `string` | Expands a three-digit hex colour to six digits, so `#123` becomes `#112233`. |
| `RGB_to_HTML(rgb)` | `string` | Converts `rgb(r, g, b)` to an uppercase hex colour. |
| `RGBPercent_to_HTML(rgb)` | `string` | Converts `rgb(r%, g%, b%)` to an uppercase hex colour. |
| `HSL_to_HTML(hsl)` | `string` | Converts `hsl(h, s%, l%)` to an uppercase hex colour. |
| `HWB_to_HTML(hwb)` | `string` | Converts `hwb(h w% b%)` to an uppercase hex colour. |
| `named_to_HTML(name)` | `string` | Converts a CSS named colour to an uppercase hex colour. The match ignores case. |
| `to_html(code, format)` | `string` | Converts a colour by its format name: `hwb`, `hsl`, `rgb`, `rgb_percent`, `hex`, or `named`. |
| `get_colour(attrs, default)` | `string` or `nil` | Reads `colour` from the attributes, then `color`, and returns `default` when neither is set. |
| `is_custom_colour(colour)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the value is a custom colour rather than a named one. Use it to choose between a class and an inline style. |
| `hue_to_rgb(p, q, t)` | `number` | A helper for `HSL_to_HTML`, which returns one RGB component. |

: Functions of `colour.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,15,55]"}

## content-extraction.lua

Finds sections, divs, and headers in a list of Pandoc blocks.
It needs `string.lua` and `html.lua`.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extract_section(blocks, section_id, include_header)` | blocks or `nil` | Returns the blocks of the section with that header identifier, up to the next header of the same or a higher level. The header is included unless `include_header` is `false`. |
| `remove_sections(blocks, predicate)` | kept, removed | Removes each section whose header matches `predicate`. Returns the kept blocks and the removed blocks, in document order. The input is not changed. |
| `extract_div(blocks, div_id, include_div)` | blocks or `nil` | Searches inside the blocks for a Div with that identifier, and returns its contents. The Div itself is included when `include_div` is `true`. |
| `find_block(blocks, predicate)` | integer or `nil` | Returns the index of the first block for which `predicate` is true. |
| `protect_headers(blocks, id_prefix, format)` | blocks | Replaces each header with a raw HTML block, so its identifier cannot clash with another. The optional prefix is added to each identifier. |
| `parse_sections(blocks)` | table | Splits content at a horizontal rule into `header_text`, `header_level`, `body_blocks`, and `footer_blocks`. Useful for modal dialogs. |
| `extract_code_metadata(code_text, pattern)` | filename or `nil`, text | Reads a line such as `python \| filename: script.py`, and returns the filename and the code without that line. |

: Functions of `content-extraction.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[32,18,50]"}

## embedded.lua

Loads a filter that an extension bundles, and skips it when the project has its own copy of the same extension.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `load(name, file)` | table | Loads the bundled filter at `file`, unless the project has its own copy of the extension `name`. Returns the list of filters, which is empty when the bundled one is skipped. |

: Functions of `embedded.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,15,55]"}

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_repository()` | `string` or `nil` | Returns `owner/repo`, read from the `origin` remote, or `nil` when there is none. |

## html.lua

Builds raw HTML, and adds an HTML dependency to the page once.
It needs `string.lua`.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw_header(level, text, id, classes, attributes)` | `string` | Returns a raw HTML header element, with its identifier, classes, and any extra attributes. |
| `get_extension_version()` | `string` | Returns the `version` of the running extension, read from its `_extension.yml`. Raises an error when that file has no version. |
| `ensure_html_dependency(config)` | `boolean` | Adds an HTML dependency once per document, and returns `true` only when it was added. Without `version` in `config`, the running extension's version is used. |
| `reset_dependencies()` | nothing | Forgets the dependencies added so far. Use it when one process renders several documents. |

: Functions of `html.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[38,15,47]"}

## logging.lua

Writes messages in one format, prefixed with the extension name: `[extension-name] Message`.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `log_error(extension_name, message)` | nothing | Writes an error message. |
| `log_warning(extension_name, message)` | nothing | Writes a warning message. |
| `log_output(extension_name, message)` | nothing | Writes an informational message. |
| `log_debug(extension_name, message)` | nothing | Writes a debug message. |

: Functions of `logging.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[38,15,47]"}

## lookup.lua

Checks membership in a list, and maps keywords to values.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is_valid_value(value, valid_array, formatter)` | `string` or `nil` | Returns the value, formatted when `formatter` is given, if it is in `valid_array`. Returns `nil` when it is not. A `formatter` string is a prefix, and a function receives the value. |
| `in_array(value, valid_array)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the value is in the array. |
| `keyword_to_value(keyword, mapping, default)` | `string` | Returns the mapped value of the keyword. Falls back to `default`, and then to the keyword itself. |
| `size_to_css(size)` | `string` | Converts a size keyword such as `large` to `font-size: 1.2em;`. A value that already has a unit is passed through. Returns an empty string for an empty input. |

: Functions of `lookup.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[38,15,47]"}

## metadata.lua

Reads the configuration of an extension from the document metadata, and the project metadata from Quarto.
It needs `string.lua` and `logging.lua`.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_extension_config(meta, extension_name)` | any or `nil` | Returns the table under `extensions.<extension_name>`. |
| `get_metadata_value(meta, extension_name, key)` | `string` or `nil` | Returns `extensions.<extension_name>.<key>` as a string. A boolean `false` is a value, and is returned as `"false"`. |
| `check_deprecated_config(meta, extension_name, key, deprecation_warning_shown)` | value or `nil`, `boolean` | Reads a top-level key that an extension has deprecated, and warns once. Returns the value and the updated warning flag. |
| `get_option_with_fallbacks(spec)` | any | Returns one option, taking the first of the named arguments, the document metadata, and the default. |
| `get_options(spec)` | table | Returns several options at once, by the same rule as `get_option_with_fallbacks`. |
| `get_project_metadata()` | table or `nil`, reason, path | Reads the `format.metadata` table that Quarto writes to `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO`. When that fails, the reason is one of `file is unreadable`, `file is empty`, `invalid JSON`, or `no format.metadata table`. |
| `get_project_repo_url(format_meta)` | `string` or `nil` | Returns `repo-url` from the website or book metadata, website first. |

: Functions of `metadata.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[38,20,42]"}

## pandoc-helpers.lua

Builds Pandoc elements, and checks the Lua values Pandoc hands to a filter.
It needs `string.lua`.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_link(text, uri)` | `pandoc.Link` or `nil` | Returns a link, or `nil` when the text or the URI is empty. |
| `attr(id, classes, attributes)` | `pandoc.Attr` | Returns the Pandoc attributes built from an identifier, classes, and key-value pairs. |
| `has_class(classes, name)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the class list holds `name`. |
| `add_class(classes, name)` | nothing | Adds `name` to the class list, when it is not already there. |
| `get_quarto_format()` | `string`, `string` | Returns the output format, such as `html`, `typst`, or `pptx`, or `unknown`, and its language. |
| `is_object_empty(obj)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the value is `nil`, an empty string, or an empty table. |
| `is_type_simple(obj)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the value is a string, a number, or a boolean. |
| `is_function_userdata(obj)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the value is a function or userdata. |
| `get_value(fields, obj)` | any | Reads a nested value, following the field names in order. |
| `attributes_to_table(element)` | table | Converts the attributes of a Div, Span, Table, or Image to a plain table. |

: Functions of `pandoc-helpers.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[38,20,42]"}

## paths.lua

Resolves paths against the project, and checks file types.
It needs `string.lua`.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resolve_project_path(path)` | `string` | Resolves a path relative to the project directory. A leading `/` marks the path as project-relative. Without a project, the leading `/` is removed. |
| `has_extension(uri, extensions, case_sensitive)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the URI ends with one of the extensions. The match ignores case unless `case_sensitive` is `true`, and the leading dot is optional. |
| `is_markdown(uri)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the URI ends with `.md`, `.markdown`, or `.qmd`. |

: Functions of `paths.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[38,15,47]"}

## schema-check.lua

Checks a document, a shortcode call, a code cell, and an output format against the extension's `_schema.yml`.
It needs `logging.lua` and `string.lua`.

The validator is passed to the module as an argument, not loaded by it.
An extension can then vendor the schema validator from one source and this module from another.
The validator must provide `load_schema`, `validate`, `validate_shortcode`, `extract_meta_options`, `validate_attributes`, `validate_format`, and `validate_cells`.
The last one needs Quarto Wizard schema 2.3.0 or newer.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new(validator, extension_name, schema_path)` | checker | Reads the schema once, and returns a checker. The schema is `_schema.yml` beside the entry point. Pass `schema_path` when the entry point is in a subdirectory, such as `'../_schema.yml'`. |
| `checker:options(meta)` | defaults, resolved | Checks the document options. Returns a copy of the schema defaults first. Second, returns `resolved`: `provided` holds what the document set, `merged` holds those values with coercion and defaults applied, and `defaults` holds the schema defaults. `resolved` is `nil` when there is no schema. Only the first call reads `meta`. |
| `checker:option(key)` | value | Returns what the schema resolves one option to, after `options` has run. |
| `checker:attributes(attributes, group)` | table | Checks the attributes of one element against the `attributes` section, and returns the resolved values. The element's own group and `_any` both apply. |
| `checker:cells(options, language)` | table | Checks the comment-pipe options of a code cell, such as `#\|`, against the `cells` section. The cell language picks the group. |
| `checker:format(name)` | table | Checks one output format against the `formats` section, after `options` has run. |
| `checker:call(name, args, kwargs)` | nothing | Checks one shortcode call against the shortcode's entry in the schema, and reports what it finds. The rendered output does not change. |

: Functions of `schema-check.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[38,20,42]"}

Build the checker at file scope, and not inside a shortcode handler.
The schema is then read once for the render, and not once for each call.

```lua
local check = require(quarto.utils.resolve_path('_vendor/quarto-lua-modules/schema-check.lua'):gsub('%.lua$', ''))
local checker = check.new(validator, 'iconify')
local defaults, resolved = checker:options(meta)
```

## string.lua

Tests, splits, trims, and escapes strings.
It has no dependencies.

| Function | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is_empty(s)` | `boolean` | Tells whether the value is `nil` or an empty string. |
| `escape_pattern(s)` | `string` | Escapes the characters that have a meaning in a Lua pattern. |
| `split(str, sep)` | table | Splits the string at each match of `sep`. |
| `trim(str)` | `string` | Removes leading and trailing whitespace. |
| `to_string(val)` | `string` or `nil` | Converts any value to a string, including Pandoc objects. Returns `nil` for an empty value. |
| `strip_surrounding(text)` | prefix, inner, suffix | Removes one balanced pair of brackets or quotes, or trailing punctuation, from the ends of the text. |
| `strip_edges(text)` | prefix, inner, suffix | Removes any run of opening brackets from the start, and any run of closing brackets or punctuation from the end. |
| `find_bracketed_content(text, start_pos)` | prefix, content, suffix, position | Finds the first balanced bracket pair after `start_pos`, and splits the text around it. |
| `escape_latex(text)` | `string` | Escapes the characters that LaTeX treats as special. |
| `escape_typst(text)` | `string` | Escapes the characters that Typst treats as special. |
| `escape_typst_string(text)` | `string` | Escapes text for a Typst string literal, inside double quotes. |
| `escape_js_string(text)` | `string` | Escapes text for a JavaScript string literal. It also escapes `</`, so the text cannot close an inline script. |
| `escape_lua_pattern(text)` | `string` | Escapes text for use in `string.gsub`. |
| `escape_html(text)` | `string` | Escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'`. |
| `escape_attribute(value)` | `string` | Escapes the characters that would end an HTML attribute value. |
| `escape_text(text, format)` | `string` | Escapes text for `latex`, `typst`, or `lua`. Any other format name raises an error. |
| `ascii_id(text)` | `string` | Makes an HTML identifier from text, by lowercasing it and replacing the spaces. |

: Functions of `string.lua`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[34,20,46]"}
